🎵 Spotify to MP3 / WAV
⚠ Experimental — Paste a Spotify track link below to convert it to audio. Note: WAV is lossless (higher quality) but takes up much more storage than MP3 — roughly 5–10× the size. MP3 is plenty for most listening.
🔗 Expand URL
Paste a short Spotify link (open.spotify.com/s/...) to get the full track URL for MP3 converters. Note: If you already have the full track URL (open.spotify.com/track/...), Expand URL isn’t needed—but still useful as a fallback if Spotify switches back to short URLs.
🎬 YouTube to MP3
Paste any YouTube URL to convert it to MP3. Opens a converter in a new tab — download the file, then import it with + Add songs ▾ → + Files.
💡 Converter recommendation
Management's personal pick for YouTube-to-MP3: YTMP3 (ytmp3.cc) — a fast, free, and reliable YouTube to MP3 converter. If the built-in converter doesn't work for a video, try YTMP3 as a fallback.
🎞️ MP4 to WAV Converter
⚠ Experimental — Convert MP4 video files to WAV audio directly in your browser. No upload needed, everything stays on your device.
How to get a song
1. Tap Get song — Spotify opens with the song.
2. In Spotify, tap Share → Copy link to copy the short URL.
3. Paste the link into Expand URL above to get the full track URL. (Skip if you already have the full track URL — but still useful as a fallback if Spotify switches back to short links.)
4. Paste the expanded URL into any Spotify-to-MP3 converter and download.
5. Use + Add songs ▾ → + Files to import it.
💡 Converter recommendation
Management's personal picks for Spotify-to-MP3: Spotisaver and SpotMate — a very versatile all-rounder Spotify-to-MP3 downloader that's also compatible with other music apps.

📱 Transfer to a new device
Your premium is tied to this device. To move it to a new phone:

1. On your old phone, go to Library → Export and save the backup file.
2. On your new phone, install SideCut and go to Library → Import.
3. Select the backup file — your premium, library, playlists, and pinned artists will all transfer.

Your premium code is embedded in the export, so it automatically activates on the new device. You can then remove premium from the old device using the button below.

Get Songs
Convert short Spotify links (open.spotify.com/s/...) into full track URLs (open.spotify.com/track/...) that work with MP3 converters. This is the free way to get songs into your library — no premium needed.

How to get a song into your library:
1. In Spotify, tap Share → Copy link on any song.
2. Paste the short link into the box below and tap Expand. (If you already have the full track URL — open.spotify.com/track/... — this step isn’t needed, but still useful if Spotify changes their URL format.)
3. Copy the expanded URL and paste it into any Spotify-to-MP3 converter to download the file.
4. Tap + Add songs ▾ → + Files and pick the downloaded MP3s — they're stored locally on your device.

The whole tutorial in text:
•Getting music in: SideCut plays audio files saved on your device. The free way: Spotify → Share → Copy link → paste into Expand URL → take the full link to any Spotify-to-MP3 converter → import the MP3s with + Add songs ▾ → + Files. + Add folder grabs a whole folder; Import library restores a backup .zip.
•Playing: tap any song to play it; use the mini player at the bottom for play/pause, skip, and shuffle. Tap the ⋮ next to a song for more options.
•Jump to the playing song: tap the record on the mini player — it opens the full now-playing view and scrolls straight to that song. No need to hunt for it.
•Look: Settings → Theme for looks, Glow for edge lines and glow, Playback for crossfade/gapless, Equalizer for 8-band EQ.
•Organizing: create playlists from the Playlists tab, add songs via the ⋮ menu, long-press a row to select multiple tracks, and Export library to back everything up as a .zip.
•Notifications: the media player in your phone\'s notification shade plays/pauses but tapping it won\'t open SideCut — open the app manually to get back to the song list.
Works offline
Once your songs are imported, SideCut keeps running with no connection:
Yes — playing your library, playlists, shuffle/repeat, EQ, DJ mode, seek, sleep timer, gapless, crossfade, lyrics you've already fetched, all saved settings, and every Sandbox tweak (custom quick actions, Home layout).
Needs internet — Discover (song search, previews, pinned artists, new-release checks), fetching new lyrics or covers, and update checks. Your actual music files always play straight from this device.
Need help? Try the 🤖 AI Assistant in Settings → Support — it knows everything about SideCut and works instantly offline. If the AI can't help, contact us at sidecutsupport@gmail.com (Settings → Support).
Accepted file types
Audio: .mp3, .m4a, .wav, .flac, .ogg, .aac, .wma, .opus, .aiff, .alac
Other: .zip (library/playlist import), .csv (Spotify playlist import)
Read this before using SideCut.
SideCut has themes, glow effects, and an RGB color mode that produce flashing, pulsing, and rapidly changing colors — including along the edges of your screen while music plays.
A very small number of people may experience seizures or loss of consciousness when exposed to certain flashing lights or patterns, even with no history of seizures or epilepsy.
If you have photosensitive epilepsy, or have ever had a seizure triggered by flashing lights, turn these effects off:
•Avoid the RGB, RGB+, and animated dynamic themes (Aurora, Synthwave, Ocean, Ember, Galaxy, Cyberpunk, Glacier).
•In Glow settings, leave the edge lines, blur bands, and corner glow off.
•Use a static theme (Rose Gold, Violet, Onyx, etc.) and the DJ Mode visuals with caution.
•Sandbox → Reduce motion disables all animations and transitions across the app.
Stop using the app and consult a doctor if you experience dizziness, altered vision, eye or muscle twitching, loss of awareness, or disorientation while using it. Keep a safe distance from the screen and play in a well-lit room.

Enabled
Rolling back swaps the app to a saved copy of an older version that lives as a separate, self-contained snapshot on this device — the actual SideCut app installed on your device (and its cached shell) stays exactly as it is; only what this tab shows changes. Your library and settings live in their own storage, untouched by the switch.
⚠ Before you roll back
Older versions can have side effects: data loss or a broken app that won\'t open or run correctly. If that happens you'll need to clear app data to recover, which wipes your library. Back up your library first — use Export library to save a .zip you can restore after clearing data. Don't roll back without a backup.
SideCut v48
Understanding the version numbers
Turn DJ Mode off for any individual playlist — handy for religious or devotional playlists you'd rather listen to as-is. Built-in names (Paath, Gurbani, Kirtaan, Dhadi Jhatta, Gurmukhi, Religious, Prayer) are always off and shown locked below.
A few built-in behaviors worth knowing:
•Hold the mini record player to adjust its angle. Long-press the little turntable at the bottom of the screen — a Turntable angle popup opens with TILT / SPIN / ROLL sliders. Drag them while the preview moves live; Reset brings back the default look. A quick tap still jumps to the playing song.
•DJ Mode is disabled for certain playlists. If a playlist is named Paath, Gurbani, Kirtaan, Dhadi Jhatta, Gurmukhi, Religious, or Prayer — uppercase or lowercase, it doesn't matter — DJ Mode steps aside for that playlist. You can also turn DJ Mode off manually for any playlist from DJ Mode per playlist above — handy for religious or devotional playlists you'd rather listen to as-is. You'll see a small note when this happens.
•Your music stays on your device. SideCut plays files you import — it never uploads them. Fetching new lyrics or covers, and update checks, are the only things that need internet.
•Update timestamps are in Eastern Time. Every changelog entry shows its date and time in ET (EDT in summer, EST in winter) — never UTC.
•Jump to the playing song from anywhere. Tap the record on the mini player at the bottom — it opens the full now-playing view and scrolls straight to that song, so you never have to hunt for it in a playlist.
•The phone's media player can't open SideCut. The notification-shade / lock-screen player can play, pause, and skip — but tapping it won\'t open the app. To get back to the song list, open SideCut from your launcher.
•Lyrics auto-scroll isn't perfect. Timed lyrics are matched to a best-effort sync, so the highlight can drift — tap Auto-scroll in the lyrics view to turn it off and read at your own pace.
•Back up before rolling back. Older app versions can break things or lose data. Use Export library to save a .zip first, since recovering from a bad rollback may require clearing app data.

How to use SideCut

Getting music into your library
SideCut plays audio files saved on your device — it doesn't stream or fetch anything itself. The free way to get a song from Spotify (no premium needed):
1.In Spotify, tap Share → Copy link on any song to copy the short link.
2.Paste it into Expand URL (Settings → Expand URL, or the box at the top of Discover) — it becomes the full track URL that converters accept. (Already have the full URL? You can skip this, but it’s handy if Spotify changes their link format.)
3.Paste the expanded URL into any Spotify-to-MP3 converter and download the file.
4.Back in SideCut, tap + Add songs ▾ → + Files and pick the downloaded MP3s — they're now stored locally on your device.
•+ Add folder grabs a whole folder at once — handy for a full album or your Downloads folder
•Import library restores a full backup .zip, including playlists and tags
Playing music
•Tap any song in your list to start playing it
•Use the mini player at the bottom for play/pause, skip, and shuffle
•Tap the record on the mini player to open the full now-playing view and jump straight to the song that's playing — no scrolling needed
•Tap the ⋮ (kebab) next to a song for more options — add to playlist, play next, delete, and more
Customizing the look
•Open Settings (gear icon) → Theme to pick a look
•Under Settings → Glow, mix and match edge lines, blur bands, and corner glow — all independent toggles, all customizable
•Settings → Playback has crossfade, gapless mode, and normalization
•Settings → Equalizer has 8 adjustable bands plus presets
Playlists & organizing
•Create playlists from the Playlists tab, then add songs via the kebab menu on any track
•Long-press a song row to select multiple tracks at once
•Export library anytime to back everything up as a .zip you can restore later
